profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility ORD12, at 9333 West Grand Avenue, Franklin Park, IL 60131. Digital Realty's own property listing for ORD12, fetched this session, lists the building at 110,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint, a cluster of suburban buildings near O'Hare International Airport in Franklin Park and neighboring Elk Grove Village, in addition to the much larger Lakeside Technology Center downtown at 350 East Cermak Road. Digital Realty markets its Chicago properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Chicago buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage. Illinois has offered data center-specific state tax incentives, administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, that local officials have credited with helping draw large colocation and hyperscale investment to the Chicago metro.

reading.body:
Digital Realty ORD12 is a 110,000 square foot colocation building in Franklin Park, Illinois, near O'Hare International Airport, part of Digital Reality's Chicago metro cluster. Digital Realty does not publish an IT megawatt capacity figure for this building on its property page or in its 2025 10-K filing. Without a stated power rating, the facility's compute density cannot be estimated.

Chicago is one of Digital Realty's largest US colocation footprints, anchored by the Lakeside Technology Center downtown and supported by suburban properties near O'Hare in Franklin Park and Elk Grove Village. ComEd serves most of the metro. Illinois offers data center-specific state tax incentives that state officials credit with attracting large operators to the region. Of 44 mapped data center facilities in Illinois, only 6 publish megawatt figures; the state total of published capacity is 236 MW.

This facility's significance to AI depends on its tenant mix and power draw, neither of which are published. ORD12's position in Chicago's colocation ecosystem, combined with the metro's dense interconnection and proximity to core US internet exchange points, positions it as infrastructure for enterprise and cloud tenants, but its role in AI workloads cannot be determined from the specifications available.
